notes:
Summary: Mid-market customer building AI-first customer support chat (in-product + web chat). Interested in Redwood Hosted API for fast time-to-value, but wants path to Dedicated once we prove latency/cost. Primary goal: streaming responses + tool calling to ticketing system (Zendesk) and KB.

Key quote: "We need streaming that feels instant to users — first token under 1.5s or the product team will push back." — Maya Singh, Head of Product.

Technical constraints / requirements:
- Latency SLO: first-token <1.5s 95th pct across sessions (target during peak: <1.2s).
- Throughput: expected 800–1,200 concurrent chats during peak, ~250k messages/month initially.
- Streaming required (websocket or SSE) for typing/partial replies.
- Tool calling: must call Zendesk API, internal KB search, and optionally a small code-runner for templates.
- Fallbacks: want automatic fallback to smaller model if latency spikes, but preserve function/tool calls.
- Data residency: US-only legal requirement for PII in tickets.
- Retention and audit: 1 year retention, full audit logs for all API calls.
- Security: Enterprise SSO (SAML), KMS integration for keying at rest.

Commercial notes:
- Price sensitivity: mid-market budget; acceptable ARR $75k–$200k depending on committed volume.
- They prefer a staged commercial model: start hosted (consumption), then switch to reserved Dedicated (commit) if POC meets SLOs.

Engagement timeline / talking points so far:
- 2025-11-04: initial inbound demo request (AE Daniel).
- 2025-11-11: discovery call — product + infra. Notes: high emphasis on streaming UX and predictable latency.
- 2025-12-02: hosted API technical deep-dive with SE (Laura). Covered streaming SDKs, webhooks, tool calling patterns.
- 2026-01-09: security questionnaire submitted (SOC2, ISO questions). They flagged KMS + audit log granularity.
- 2026-01-20: pricing call — they asked for 12-month committed vs burst pricing scenarios.
- 2026-02-10: demo of streaming with small prototype (proof-of-concept) — they liked KV cache behavior but want firmer FTF numbers.
- 2026-02-28: agreed to 2-week POC on Hosted API (dev org + 10 pilot agents). POC acceptance criteria defined (see below).

POC acceptance criteria (customer-provided):
- 2-week pilot with 10 live agents answering real tickets.
- First-token latency 95th percentile <1.5s during pilot business hours.
- Streaming integration stable over websocket for 8-hour load windows.
- Tool calling success rate >99% (Zendesk + KB).
- Logs + audit export available to their SIEM.

Open items / blockers:
- Need SOC2 artifact (in progress). Sales legal needs to agree SLA addendum for first-token SLO.
- Confirm region-specific data handling (US-only). Engineering wants sample telemetry for median/95th latency on current hosted cluster.
- Verify streaming SDK compatibility with their React-based chat widget (they use custom websocket client).

Comm plan / next steps:
- SE (Laura) to run synthetic load script week of 2026-03-03 to simulate peak concurrency and capture latency breakdowns.
- Provide SOC2 report + security FAQ link to customer (drive link above).
- Draft Hosted POC statement of work (2 weeks) and measurement dashboard.
- If POC meets SLOs, commercial to propose Dedicated pricing with monthly reserved slots and burst pool.

Sales snippets / internal notes:
- Customer profile: product-led support team, emphasis on UX and latency. Likely to convert to Dedicated if economics + SLOs align.
- Upsell paths: Optimize (batching/caching suggestions) once in Dedicated to lower per-ticket cost.
- Risk: If hosted latency can't meet <1.5s FTF at 95p, they will look at self-hosted vendors or building in-house streaming optimizations.
